# Phase 1 — the flood definition, and how well it holds up

*Generated by `hydrocascade report` on 2026-09-05. Every number below is recomputed from the pipeline; nothing is transcribed.*

Region `chaliyar_pilot` · period 2018-06-01 to 2024-12-31 · 9,038 reaches · analysis CRS EPSG:32643

> ### ⚠ The discharge is synthetic
>
> `data_mode.glofas` is `synthetic`, so the numbers in sections 2, 3 and 5
> describe a stand-in generator, not the GloFAS reanalysis. They are here to
> show that the procedure runs end to end and that the diagnostics fire; they
> are **not results and must not be quoted**. Sections 1 and 4 are independent
> of the discharge source and stand as they are.
>
> Switching `data_mode.glofas: real` in `config/default.yaml` and supplying a
> Copernicus CDS key turns every one of them into a result with no code change.

## 1. The rule

Doc 02 §3.1, implemented in `src/hydrocascade/ingest/floods.py`. It is a procedure with no judgement calls in it, which is the point: four people running it get the same catalog.

| Step | What happens | Config key | Value in force |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Annual maxima of daily discharge per reach | `period` | full record 1980-01-01 to 2024-12-31 |
| 2 | Fit **Gumbel by L-moments**, read Q2, Q5, Q20 | `floods.return_periods` | [2, 5, 20] |
| 3 | An event opens on the first day Q exceeds the threshold | `floods.threshold_return_period` | Q2 |
| 4 | The episode closes after N consecutive days below it | `floods.decluster_days` | 3 days |
| 5 | Only reaches above the eligibility area are detected on | `floods.min_contributing_area_km2` | 50 km² |
| 6 | Mark `m_F = log(Q_peak / Q2)`; class from the Q2/Q5/Q20 bands | — | — |

**Why L-moments and not maximum likelihood.** A record containing 2018 and 2024 has two enormous annual maxima. Maximum likelihood lets them drag the fitted scale; L-moments are built from order statistics and barely move. This is also GloFAS's own threshold procedure, so adopting it means our flood definition matches an operational system instead of being invented for this project.

**Why declustering is not optional.** Without it a single week-long flood counts as five events at the same reach, which inflates exactly the self-excitation the model is supposed to measure. Three sub-threshold days is the Doc 02 §3.1 step 3 rule.

**Eligibility.** 1,811 of 9,038 reaches clear 50 km². Operational GloFAS reporting points are restricted to catchments above 250 km²; 50 km² is the research-mode compromise Doc 02 §3.1 step 5 allows, and §3 requires the 250 km² check that section 3 below runs.

## 2. What the rule produced

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| flood events in the study period | **9,005** |
| reaches with at least one event | 1,794 of 1,811 eligible |
| exceedance rate | 0.72 events per reach-year (Q2 implies 0.69) |
| median days above threshold per event | 2 |
| severity split | 6,871 minor · 1,732 major · 402 extreme |
| Q2 per reach (reaches with events) | median 738.0 m³/s, range 283.0–6,638.8 |
| events outside the study period (threshold-fitting record only) | 48,548 |

**The rate is the diagnostic to read first**, because it is fixed by the return period alone. If episodes above Q2 arrive as a Poisson process with rate λ, the annual maximum stays below Q2 with probability `exp(−λ)`, and the return period pins that at `1 − 1/2` — so λ = −ln(1 − 1/2) = **0.69** events per reach-year, not 1.0. This run gives **0.72**, a ratio of 1.03. A rate far from the theoretical one indicts the discharge series, not the detection rule, and `floods.detect_for_all_reaches` warns when the ratio leaves 0.4–2.5.

**Events per year**

| year | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| events | 904 | 1,088 | 1,397 | 2,575 | 367 | 455 | 2,219 |

## 3. Sensitivity — Doc 02 §3.5

Each variant re-runs the whole procedure on the same discharge table. Doc 11 §5 rule 3 says a variant is a config edit, not a code edit, so `corroboration.sensitivity` builds a modified config and calls the same detector the headline run uses — there is no second implementation to drift out of sync.

| Variant | Eligible reaches | Events | Reaches hit | Rate /reach-yr | minor / major / extreme |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| headline (Q2, 3 d, 50 km²) | 1,811 | **9,005** | 1,794 | 0.72 | 6,871 / 1,732 / 402 |
| threshold Q5 instead of Q2 | 1,811 | **2,141** | 1,201 | 0.25 | 0 / 1,739 / 402 |
| declustering 5 d instead of 3 d | 1,811 | **8,855** | 1,794 | 0.71 | 6,722 / 1,731 / 402 |
| eligibility 250 km² instead of 50 km² | 587 | **2,957** | 581 | 0.73 | 2,255 / 585 / 117 |

- **threshold Q5 instead of Q2**: 2,141 events, -76% against the headline.
- **declustering 5 d instead of 3 d**: 8,855 events, -2% against the headline.
- **eligibility 250 km² instead of 50 km²**: 2,957 events, -67% against the headline.

Two things in that table look like bugs and are not.

- **The Q5 row has no `minor` events.** `severity_class` is defined by the Q2/Q5/Q20 bands (Doc 02 §3.1 step 4) and `minor` means Q2–Q5. Detecting at Q5 means every event is at least Q5 by construction, so the `minor` bin is necessarily empty. The severity scale stays anchored to Q2 even when the detection threshold moves, which is what keeps marks comparable across variants.
- **Each variant's rate is close to its own theoretical value, not to the others.** Q2 implies 0.69 events per reach-year and Q5 implies 0.22. A variant whose rate tracked the headline's instead would be the thing to worry about.

Doc 02 §3.5 asks whether the *sign and significance of the cross-hazard coupling* change under these variants. That question cannot be answered until the coupling is fitted in Phase 4. What Phase 1 owes is the machinery and the event counts, which is what this table is; the Phase 5 ablation reruns the fit on each variant catalog.

## 4. The blind spot — Doc 02 §3.4, checked rather than repeated

Doc 02 §3.4 states up front that the Punnapuzha at Chooralmala has a contributing area *far below* the eligibility threshold, so the discharge rule cannot see the flood at the debris-flow site. We now have the catchment, so the claim can be verified instead of restated.

| | reach | catchment | eligible at 50 km²? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mundakkai injection point | `R-02503` | 2.3 km² | **no** |
| Punnapuzha at the Chooralmala bridge | `R-01977` | 21.4 km² | **no** |

The bridge landmark snaps to its reach at 571 m. **Doc 02 §3.4 is confirmed at both thresholds**, though the margin is worth stating precisely rather than repeating the word *far*: the Punnapuzha here drains 21.4 km², which is 2.3× below our research-mode 50 km² bar and 12× below the 250 km² bar operational GloFAS reporting points actually use. The injection point itself, at 2.3 km², is not close to either.

**Where the rule regains sight.** Following the chain downstream from the injection point:

| eligibility | first visible reach | its catchment | reaches blind before it | travel time from the injection point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 km² | `R-01788` | 73 km² | 14 | 0.9 h |
| 250 km² | `R-02674` | 258 km² | 44 | 2.7 h |

This is the quantitative form of the limitation, and it belongs in the paper exactly like this. For the Wayanad backtest the model's predicted intensity at the headwater reaches can be validated only qualitatively — did risk rise in the right place at the right time — and quantitatively only from the first eligible reach downstream. Hiding that would be the fastest way to lose a reviewer.

## 5. Corroboration — Doc 02 §3.3

The definition is model-derived, so Doc 02 §3.3 requires it to be scored against observations. Two numbers, two statuses.

### 5.1 Precision — Sentinel-1 inundation *(FR-05)*

*Of the events the rule flags, what fraction show a real inundation signal?*

Doc 11 FR-05 names this report as the place the number is reported and an automated check as its verification. **Status: BLOCKED** — not estimated, not approximated, not filled in with a plausible figure. FR-05 is therefore recorded as unmet, which is a truthful state for a requirement to be in.

```
The Sentinel-1 precision test (Doc 02 §3.3 step 4) needs Google Earth Engine.
  1. register at https://code.earthengine.google.com
  2. pip install earthengine-api && earthengine authenticate
  3. set data_mode.sentinel1: real in config/default.yaml

The recipe is fixed, so wiring it up is mechanical:

Sentinel-1 GRD, IW mode, VV polarisation, from the COPERNICUS/S1_GRD collection.
For each detected flood event:
  1. flood image  = median composite of scenes within +/-3 days of the event date
  2. reference    = median composite over the driest month of the same relative
                    orbit (January-February for Kerala)
  3. threshold    = Otsu on the histogram of the flood-image VV backscatter,
                    computed inside the reach buffer, not globally
  4. water mask   = VV < threshold, with slope > 5 deg masked out (radar shadow)
  5. signal       = flooded area(flood) - flooded area(reference), inside a
                    1 km buffer of the reach
An event 'shows a real inundation signal' when that difference is positive and
exceeds the reference-date noise level. Reported accuracy of this method for
Kerala is around 94% overall (Doc 02 §3.2).
```

> **not publishable: the discharge is SYNTHETIC, so this measures the harness rather than GloFAS; and 6 of 6 scored rows are still sourced to the project brief rather than to a primary KSDMA / EMS / CWC record.**

A reference flood counts as detected when **any** reach in the basin recorded an event within the window. That is deliberately basin-scale: published accounts name a town, not a reach, and inventing a reach id for them would be worse than measuring a coarser quantity honestly.

The list lives in `data/reference/documented_floods.csv`. It is scored against, never fitted to. Rows without a `source_url` are ignored on the same FR-04 rule the catalog uses — a row nobody can trace is not evidence.

## 6. What turns this into the paper's version

| Blocker | Unblocked by | Turns into |
|---|---|---|
| synthetic discharge | a free Copernicus CDS account and `data_mode.glofas: real` | every count in §2, §3 and §5.2 |
| no SAR precision | a Google Earth Engine account and `data_mode.sentinel1: real` | §5.1 |
| reference list sourced to the project brief | one afternoon in the KSDMA annual reports, the Copernicus EMS activation list and the CWC portal, one `source_url` per row | a publishable §5.2 |

None of the three needs a code change. That was the design intent of `ingest/adapters.py`: the pipeline never blocks on an approval email, and it never quietly reports the stand-in as though it were the real thing.
